ISCI 201.description: Major concepts, principles, theories, issues, and trends in the development of Information Science.
ISCI 201.subject: ISCI
ISCI 201.title: Data, Information Society

ISCI 202.description: An introduction to the basic information technologies used in all types of information organizations and the essential concepts and skills needed for information literacy.
ISCI 202.subject: ISCI
ISCI 202.title: Information Literacy and Technology

ISCI 203.description: Artificial intelligence (AI) focusing on the futurology of superior intelligence, misinformation, cognitive-bias, cyber decision-making, and other information science and communication concepts.
ISCI 203.subject: ISCI
ISCI 203.title: AI: Cognitive Aspects and Social Impacts

ISCI 215.description: Ethical issues surrounding the use of data and information at the individual and organizational levels.
ISCI 215.subject: ISCI
ISCI 215.title: Ethics in the Era of Big Data

ISCI 249.description: An exploration of theoretical and practical foundations of user-centered design from both the design and research perspectives.
ISCI 249.subject: ISCI
ISCI 249.title: Principles of User Experience and Design (UX/UI)

ISCI 250.description: Overview of responsive website design, development and basic content management systems. Examine the current tools and standards and learn how they function together in a modern web environment. Emphasis on the myriad of viewing devices and specific reference to the unique needs of information intensive institutions.
ISCI 250.subject: ISCI
ISCI 250.title: Information Design

ISCI 259.description: User behavior and priorities; gather, analyze, and communicate key insights to develop effective products and services.
ISCI 259.subject: ISCI
ISCI 259.title: User Experience Research Methods and Tools

ISCI 283.description: Relevant history and practical coverage of the news media; digital participation and democratic citizenship; systems of power and oppression; how individuals and groups interpret media frames and arguments.
ISCI 283.subject: ISCI
ISCI 283.title: Battling Misinformation, Deepfakes, and Conspiracy Theories

ISCI 301.description: Introduction to the concepts, issues, theories, and techniques of information storage and retrieval systems.
ISCI 301.subject: ISCI
ISCI 301.title: Text Mining in Big Data Analytics

ISCI 310.description: Overview of major types of research methods and techniques within the field of information science. Methods of data analysis, evaluation of published research, and ethical principles.
ISCI 310.subject: ISCI
ISCI 310.title: Information Science Data Analysis and Evaluation

ISCI 315.description: Problems and ethical issues that arise in the development and implementation of information policies in Information Science.
ISCI 315.subject: ISCI
ISCI 315.title: Cyberethics and Information Policy

ISCI 316.description: Introduces blockchain technology and its applications in various professional areas, businesses, and industries. No prior blockchain knowledge is required to be successful in this foundational course.
ISCI 316.subject: ISCI
ISCI 316.title: Blockchain and Cryptocurrency

ISCI 317.description: Introduces bitcoin, cryptocurrency, data privacy, self-sovereign identity, and other blockchain concepts and applications with in the context of professional areas, businesses, and industries. No prior blockchain knowledge is required to be successful in this foundational course.
ISCI 317.subject: ISCI
ISCI 317.title: Blockchain, Privacy, and Decentralization

ISCI 325.description: A study of materials for children from birth through elementary school (age 13) with emphasis on the evaluation, selection, and use of those materials to meet the educational, cultural, and recreational needs of children.
ISCI 325.subject: ISCI
ISCI 325.title: Children’s Literature

ISCI 330.description: The basic information technology concepts and applications relevant to library and related information environments. Unique information technology needs and applications of information-intensive organizations.
ISCI 330.subject: ISCI
ISCI 330.title: Introduction to Computer Technology Applications for Info Env

ISCI 340.description: This course provides students with essential skills and training in information and cyber security leading to the option to complete the CCSA certification process through Check Point Software Technologies.
ISCI 340.subject: ISCI
ISCI 340.title: Cyber Security and Information Science

ISCI 380.description: Examination of selected current and emerging topics in the field of information science and data analytics. May be repeated for credit as topics vary.
ISCI 380.subject: ISCI
ISCI 380.title: Special Topics in Information Science

ISCI 402.description: History, development, and implementation of theories and practices associated with managing information environments.
ISCI 402.subject: ISCI
ISCI 402.title: Management in Data Driven Organizations

ISCI 410.description: Introduction to the background, principles, practices, and technologies of knowledge management for library and information professionals.
ISCI 410.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ISCI 301.
ISCI 410.subject: ISCI
ISCI 410.title: Knowledge Work as an Organizational Asset

ISCI 415.description: Examines the design, uses, and effects of information and communication technologies (ICTs) from the standpoint that society and technology mutually shape one another.
ISCI 415.subject: ISCI
ISCI 415.title: Social Issues in Information and Communications Technologies

ISCI 420.description: An overview of the communication models, major concepts, trends, and other related issues of information transfer with a focus on information seeking and use in digital age.
ISCI 420.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ISCI 201 or JOUR 101.
ISCI 420.subject: ISCI
ISCI 420.title: Information and Communication Needs and Assessment

ISCI 429.description: Online resources specific to mass communications, research strategies, organization and creation of digital information.
ISCI 429.subject: ISCI
ISCI 429.title: Information Management for Journalists

ISCI 430.description: Processes and techniques for designing user-centered information systems on the Web. Issues of needs analysis, content development, cognitive models, human-computer interaction, interface design, and usability testing.
ISCI 430.subject: ISCI
ISCI 430.title: User-Centered Information Architecture

ISCI 434.description: The students will review knowledge discovery basics concepts, techniques, tools, and applications. This course is project based and the students will develop new Wikipedia pages by reading papers in a selected domain.
ISCI 434.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: MATH 122 or MATH 141 or MATH 142 or MATH 170 or MATH 172 or STAT 515 or STAT 201 or STAT 205.
ISCI 434.subject: ISCI
ISCI 434.title: Introduction to Knowledge Discovery

ISCI 435.description: Theoretical and technological foundations of building the digital information infrastructure. Emphasis on technical aspects of managing digital assets for Intranet and Internet use.
ISCI 435.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ISCI 202, ISCI 402.
ISCI 435.subject: ISCI
ISCI 435.title: Planning and Sustaining Digital Projects

ISCI 436.description: Emerging concepts and techniques of information science using the Python programming language.
ISCI 436.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in CSCE 104 or CSCE 106.
ISCI 436.subject: ISCI
ISCI 436.title: Using Python for Information Science

ISCI 440.description: Strategies and techniques for locating competitive intelligence information.
ISCI 440.subject: ISCI
ISCI 440.title: Competitive Intelligence

ISCI 450.description: Problem of identifying or defining cultural heritage and the issues and problems in preserving, accessing, and managing cultural heritage information. Issues such as copyright/ownership, technical problems of preservation and intellectual access, and the different ways in which libraries, archives, museums, zoos and other cultural heritage institutions operate.
ISCI 450.subject: ISCI
ISCI 450.title: Information Issues in Community Institutions

ISCI 480.description: Examination of selected current and emerging topics in the field of information science. May be repeated once for credit as topics vary.
ISCI 480.subject: ISCI
ISCI 480.title: Emerging Topics in Information Science

ISCI 494.description: Independent study in an area of information science relevant to the students professional goals. May be repeated once for credit as topics vary.
ISCI 494.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in any ISCI course.
ISCI 494.subject: ISCI
ISCI 494.title: Independent Study in Information Science

ISCI 496.description: Supervised field experience in an information agency relevant to students professional goals. Approval of the appropriate internship application must be submitted early in the semester preceding enrollment.
ISCI 496.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in any ISCI course.
ISCI 496.subject: ISCI
ISCI 496.title: Internship in Information Science

ISCI 501.description: Knowledge and skills for applying complementary technologies for learning in distributed learning environments (Pre-K-lifelong) through lecture, demonstration, and discussion.
ISCI 501.subject: ISCI
ISCI 501.title: Teaching and Training in Distributed Environments

ISCI 523.description: Media resources and techniques for children from birth to 9 years. Reading interests and developmental needs of young children. Authors, illustrators, indexes, bibliographic tools, evaluation sources, and professional literature. Not open to students enrolled in M.L.I.S. program.
ISCI 523.subject: ISCI
ISCI 523.title: Materials for Early Childhood

ISCI 525.description: Media resources for children. Reading interests of children and their curricular and independent needs for information. Authors, illustrators, indexes, bibliographic tools, and sources of evaluation of materials for children. Techniques and literature for read-aloud programs and storytelling. Not open to students enrolled in M.L.I.S. program.
ISCI 525.subject: ISCI
ISCI 525.title: Materials for Children

ISCI 527.description: Media resources for adolescents. Reading interests of adolescents and their curricular and independent information needs. Study of relationships of media to information needs and critical comparison between classic and contemporary materials for adolescents. Indexes, bibliographic tools, and sources of evaluation of materials. Not open to students enrolled in M.L.I.S. program.
ISCI 527.subject: ISCI
ISCI 527.title: Materials for Adolescents

ISCI 529.description: Specific topics of current concern to the library, information, and media professions to be identified by title. Not open to students enrolled in M.L.I.S. program.
ISCI 529.subject: ISCI
ISCI 529.title: Special Topics in Library and Information Studies

ISCI 530.description: Introductory knowledge for school library media specialists, teachers, administrators, parents, and other citizens interested in practical applications of information technology to support learning, decision making, and community building.
ISCI 530.subject: ISCI
ISCI 530.title: Applications of Information Technology and the Infrastructure

ISCI 560.description: Foster theoretical insights about data visualization. Prepare temporal, geospatial, and textual data for visual representations. In hands-on sessions, students practice data visualization techniques and apply them in a wide range of real-world scenarios.
ISCI 560.subject: ISCI
ISCI 560.title: Data Visualization

ISCI 600.description: Storytelling methods, techniques, and materials encompassing heritage, art, literature, and programming.
ISCI 600.subject: ISCI
ISCI 600.title: Storytelling: Theory, Practice, and Development

ISCI 608.description: Focuses on theories, models, and concepts of information behavior. Emphasizes information seeking and use practices and activities in relation particular communities, channels and barriers to information, and the impacts of technology. Provides an introduction to methods that can be used to study information needs, information seeking behavior, and related phenomena.
ISCI 608.subject: ISCI
ISCI 608.title: Information Behavior and Practices

ISCI 701.description: Introduction to the issues and core values of library and information professions, including equity of access, literacy and learning, information policy, collaboration, service, professional growth and development, and culturally responsive practice.
ISCI 701.subject: ISCI
ISCI 701.title: Ethics, Values, and Foundational Principles of Library and Information Science Professions

ISCI 702.description: Explores the role of library and information organizations in communities, with a focus on building community relationships, engagement, and outreach.
ISCI 702.subject: ISCI
ISCI 702.title: Community Engagement and Service

ISCI 703.description: Introduction to the design and delivery of instructional services and assistance on the use of information resources to promote information literacy and informed decision-making.
ISCI 703.subject: ISCI
ISCI 703.title: Reference and Instruction

ISCI 704.description: Introduction to the nature, development, roles, and fundamental issues of leadership in library and information organizations.
ISCI 704.subject: ISCI
ISCI 704.title: Leadership in Information Organizations

ISCI 705.description: Introduces the research process as applied to library and information science topics with an emphasis on research methods, critical evaluation, and the practical application of research.
ISCI 705.subject: ISCI
ISCI 705.title: Research Design and Evaluation

ISCI 706.description: Explores the design, use, and evaluation of information organization and retrieval systems to support digital curation and preservation, metadata generation, and information-seeking.
ISCI 706.subject: ISCI
ISCI 706.title: Information Organization and Access

ISCI 707.description: Issues and techniques of knowledge representation and information organization, information retrieval systems, and users’ information seeking behavior.
ISCI 707.subject: ISCI
ISCI 707.title: Information Organization and Retrieval

ISCI 708.description: Exploring reference principles when applied to various disciplines, populations, and contexts. Focus on topics related to information practices and behaviors of different populations, information seeking in various contexts, as well as sources of information that respond to specific subject matter, topics, or formats dictated by specific disciplinary fields.
ISCI 708.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ISCI 703.
ISCI 708.subject: ISCI
ISCI 708.title: Advanced Reference Across the Disciplines

ISCI 711.description: Nature and use of archives and records; functions of archives and records professionals; and legal, ethical, and political issues in archives and records.
ISCI 711.subject: ISCI
ISCI 711.title: Introduction to Archival Records Studies

ISCI 713.description: Exploring the role libraries play in mitigating crises, with an emphasis on crisis communication and response. Analyze real-world case studies involving libraries in contexts ranging from community-wide emergencies to individual trauma, and examine strategies organizations can use to develop effective crisis management plans. Resources and infrastructure libraries need for competent response, as well as the impact on staff, highlighting the importance of well-being in supporting communities.
ISCI 713.subject: ISCI
ISCI 713.title: Crisis Management and Communication in Libraries

ISCI 714.description: Critical analysis of current library practices through a trauma-informed lens and develop skills to advocate for organizational change that centers patron wellbeing. Special attention is given to serving vulnerable populations including children, homeless individuals, survivors of domestic violence, refugees, and those experiencing mental health challenges.
ISCI 714.subject: ISCI
ISCI 714.title: Trauma Informed Librarianship

ISCI 716.description: Introduction to analytical, descriptive, and textual bibliography, and to the principles and practice of editing.
ISCI 716.subject: ISCI
ISCI 716.title: Introduction to Bibliography and Textual Studies

ISCI 717.description: Introduction to the missions, professional standards and best practices of special collections librarianships. Topics include access and acquisitions, colletion assessment and development, collection management and maintenance, donor relations, public programming and current issues and trends. Restricted to ISCI graduate students.
ISCI 717.subject: ISCI
ISCI 717.title: Special Collections Librarianship

ISCI 718.description: Historical overview of the literary content, illustration, and social values of children’s and young adult literature written in English. Examines the influence of movements such as Romanticism, Rationalism, and postmodernism, as well as changing trends over time.
ISCI 718.subject: ISCI
ISCI 718.title: History of Children’s and Young Adult Literature

ISCI 719.description: The planning and administration of preservation programs in libraries, archives, records centers, and manuscript depositories.
ISCI 719.subject: ISCI
ISCI 719.title: Preservation Planning and Administration

ISCI 720.description: Roles, functions, and organization of school library media programs. Systematic planning and evaluation, leadership, advocacy, and integration of program into the curriculum.
ISCI 720.subject: ISCI
ISCI 720.title: School Library Media Program Development

ISCI 721.description: Problems relating to contemporary school media programs will be identified and analyzed by students, drawing from their own experiences, pertinent literature in the field, and field investigations.
ISCI 721.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ISCI 701, ISCI 703, ISCI 705, ISCI 707, ISCI 720.
ISCI 721.subject: ISCI
ISCI 721.title: Seminar in School Library Programs

ISCI 723.description: Rotating topics that provide an overview of organizational characteristics, governance, services, and distinctive features of special library types including, but not limited to, government, law, business, presidential, music, and medical libraries. Simulation of information management problems in these organizations.
ISCI 723.subject: ISCI
ISCI 723.title: Special Libraries

ISCI 725.description: History and current state of digital records, including their storage, organization, and preservation in digital libraries.
ISCI 725.subject: ISCI
ISCI 725.title: Digital Libraries

ISCI 726.description: Overview of the creation, evaluation, documentation, sharing, and application of knowledge in information organizations.
ISCI 726.subject: ISCI
ISCI 726.title: Leading Knowledge-Intensive Organizations

ISCI 728.description: Course focuses upon three topics: 1) organizational patterns for various library operations, local and regional; 2) the political environment of the public library; and 3) major problems confronting public library systems.
ISCI 728.subject: ISCI
ISCI 728.title: Public Library Systems

ISCI 729.description: An analysis of the historical development and current issues in academic libraries.
ISCI 729.subject: ISCI
ISCI 729.title: Academic Libraries

ISCI 730.description: An in-depth study of current descriptive cataloging standards covering both print and nonprint materials; searching, creating, editing, and updating encoded bibliographic records; introduction to authority records and control, subject headings, and classification.
ISCI 730.subject: ISCI
ISCI 730.title: Cataloging Information Materials

ISCI 731.description: Study of major classification and subject authority systems. Emphasizes the understanding and application of these systems in information agencies.
ISCI 731.subject: ISCI
ISCI 731.title: Subject Analysis and Classification

ISCI 733.description: An in-depth study of current descriptive cataloging standards covering both print and nonprint materials; searching, creating, editing, and updating encoded bibliographic records; introduction to authority records and control, subject headings, and classification.
ISCI 733.subject: ISCI
ISCI 733.title: E-Resources Management

ISCI 735.description: Examination of metadata definition, selection and applications; Role of metadata in information discovery, acquaintance with various metadata schemes and standards for libraries, museums, archives and info centers.
ISCI 735.subject: ISCI
ISCI 735.title: Metadata

ISCI 736.description: How to identify critical problems and propose initiatives related to library collections management, lead investigations into potential solutions, and develop project plans for implementation.
ISCI 736.subject: ISCI
ISCI 736.title: Project Management for Library Collections

ISCI 739.description: Explore current trends and methodologies in academic library instruction to design, implement, and evaluate effective library instruction sessions.
ISCI 739.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ISCI 703.
ISCI 739.subject: ISCI
ISCI 739.title: Teaching for Academic Libraries

ISCI 742.description: Role of the school library media specialist in integrating the school library media program into a K-12 standards-based curriculum, including best practices, needs assessment, collaboration, instructional design, and resource provision.
ISCI 742.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: ISCI 701, ISCI 706, ISCI 703 preferred and required education courses (for initial certification candidates).
ISCI 742.subject: ISCI
ISCI 742.title: Curricular Role of the School Librarian

ISCI 749.description: Characteristics and use of print and computer-based materials in the health sciences and for general reference librarians.
ISCI 749.subject: ISCI
ISCI 749.title: Health Sciences Information Resources

ISCI 750.description: An introduction to the role and functions of the information manager in organizations with emphases on use, retention, and management of information and records.
ISCI 750.subject: ISCI
ISCI 750.title: Information and Records Management

ISCI 751.description: Ways in which libraries and librarians become more effective providers and partners in the literacy movement.
ISCI 751.subject: ISCI
ISCI 751.title: Libraries, Literacy, and Literature

ISCI 752.description: Nontraditional library users in all types of libraries. Literacy programs, disabled and/or institutionalized persons, older adults, and members of selected ethnic groups.
ISCI 752.subject: ISCI
ISCI 752.title: Diversity in Libraries

ISCI 754.description: The nature, philosophy, and development of non-curricular programs for children and young adults in the school and public library. Among the types of programs to be discussed are storytelling, film programs, reading programs, programs for parents, and other activities associated with library service to young people. Students will study the principles and problems involved in designing, implementing, and evaluating programs of this nature.
ISCI 754.subject: ISCI
ISCI 754.title: Library Programming for Children and Young Adults

ISCI 755.description: Materials popular with adult readers, the principles and practices of reader’s advisory, and programs utilizing those materials. Emphasis on extensive reading, advisory techniques, and experience in planning and presenting engaging programs for diverse adult audiences.
ISCI 755.subject: ISCI
ISCI 755.title: Page-Turners and Programs: Engaging Adult Readers in Libraries

ISCI 756.description: A study of materials intended for children of elementary school age (6-13) with emphasis on the process of evaluating them to meet the educational, cultural, and recreational needs of children.
ISCI 756.subject: ISCI
ISCI 756.title: Children’s Materials

ISCI 757.description: A study of materials for young adults (13-19) with emphasis on the process of evaluating them to meet the educational, cultural, and recreational needs of young adults.
ISCI 757.subject: ISCI
ISCI 757.title: Young Adult Materials

ISCI 758.description: Concepts and current trends in the creation, implementation, and evaluation of adult consumer health resources and services, including consumer health informatics and e-health.
ISCI 758.subject: ISCI
ISCI 758.title: Consumer Health Resources and Information Services

ISCI 759.description: A study of picture books and audiovisual materials intended for the very young child through age 9 with emphasis on the process of evaluating these materials to meet the educational, cultural, and recreational needs of very young children.
ISCI 759.subject: ISCI
ISCI 759.title: Materials for Early Childhood

ISCI 760.description: Introduces a wide range of print and nonprint materials appropriate for Latino youth. Provides resources for librarians and educators serving young Latinos literacy needs.
ISCI 760.subject: ISCI
ISCI 760.title: Materials and Services for Latino Youth

ISCI 761.description: Technology management, use of technology and nonprint resources, and their integration into the K-12 curriculum.
ISCI 761.subject: ISCI
ISCI 761.title: Information Technologies in the School Library Program

ISCI 764.description: This course will offer an introduction to the process of selecting and evaluating materials for children and youth who are differently-able, or who have disabilities. It will also offer an introduction to the process of planning and implementing programming for these populations. Special emphasis will be placed upon Universal Design and creating inclusive environments and service learning opportunities.
ISCI 764.subject: ISCI
ISCI 764.title: Universal Design and Accessibility for Youth

ISCI 765.description: An introduction to the process of planning new and renovated spaces and facilities. Content covers roles of participants in planning preparation of building program and examines examples of recent buildings.
ISCI 765.subject: ISCI
ISCI 765.title: Planning Library Facilities

ISCI 767.description: Planning, implementation, and evaluation of public library services for children and young adults.
ISCI 767.subject: ISCI
ISCI 767.title: Management of Public Library Youth Services

ISCI 768.description: Examines in detail frequently occurring problems that require decision activity by information intensive organization managers, directors, and other administrators.
ISCI 768.subject: ISCI
ISCI 768.title: Challenges in Information Intensive Organization Administration

ISCI 769.description: Copyright policy issues affecting information professionals and institutions in the digital environment. Copyright basics, limitations and exceptions (Section 108), fair use, The Marrakesh Treaty Implementation Act (MTIA), orphan works, digital rights management, controlled digital lending (CDL), the Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA), licensing, and online learning.
ISCI 769.subject: ISCI
ISCI 769.title: Copyright in the Digital Environment: Issues for Information Professionals and Institutions

ISCI 770.description: Databases used in libraries and other information agencies, including operational and functional design. Extensive hands-on evaluation of selected database software packages.
ISCI 770.subject: ISCI
ISCI 770.title: Design and Management of Databases

ISCI 776.description: Evaluation and programming of Web technologies and related issues in libraries and in other information agencies.
ISCI 776.subject: ISCI
ISCI 776.title: Web Technologies for Information Specialists

ISCI 777.description: This course presents introductory concepts related to the creation, manipulation, and implementation of visual collections in various online environments. It identifies resources, procedures, and skills needed to successfully design, implement, and manage digital image collections in a collaborative environment.
ISCI 777.subject: ISCI
ISCI 777.title: Design and Management of Digital Image Collections

ISCI 778.description: A critical examination of the principles, trends, and issues of modern information systems design and use.
ISCI 778.subject: ISCI
ISCI 778.title: Seminar in Information Science

ISCI 779.description: This course examines the design, uses, and effects of information and communication technologies (ICTs) from the standpoint that society and technology mutually shape one another.
ISCI 779.subject: ISCI
ISCI 779.title: Social Informatics

ISCI 780.description: Identification and evaluation of information networks in libraries and other information agencies. The nature of networks, including hardware and software applications.
ISCI 780.subject: ISCI
ISCI 780.title: Information Networks

ISCI 781.description: Examines how issues of diversity, social justice, race, gender and sexuality are represented in the information professions and will study how these social imperatives affect, and are affected by, information technologies.
ISCI 781.subject: ISCI
ISCI 781.title: Critical Cultural Information Studies

ISCI 782.description: Conceptualize, critique, and reformulate social justice as an outcome while working towards a better understanding of how their social identities and systems of oppression contribute to and/or work against the social justice process.
ISCI 782.subject: ISCI
ISCI 782.title: Social Justice Storytelling and Advocacy

ISCI 783.description: Addresses the renewed phenomenon of fake news, misinformation/disinformation, and its related concepts; then focuses more explicitly on the affective information behaviors that influence our interactions with information and help us intellectually thrive in a post-truth society.
ISCI 783.subject: ISCI
ISCI 783.title: Disinformation and the Literacy Landscape

ISCI 784.description: Provides foundational knowledge and practical skills in the exploration and application of evidence-based health information systems within health information environments. Covers the principles and practices of managing health-related data, including data literacy, curation, organization, and ethical stewardship.
ISCI 784.subject: ISCI
ISCI 784.title: Health Informatics for Information Professionals

ISCI 785.description: Critical and analytical study of cyber-related leadership, information security, and information policy and ethical issues at the individual, institutional, and international levels.
ISCI 785.subject: ISCI
ISCI 785.title: Leadership and Ethics in Information Security

ISCI 787.description: Application, management and evaluation of information systems for libraries and other information agencies, including emerging technical, administrative and management issues related to these systems.
ISCI 787.subject: ISCI
ISCI 787.title: Seminar in Applied Information Systems for Information Specialists

ISCI 791.description: An intensive experience examining information systems, data management practices, and knowledge organization across different cultural and technological contexts. Students visit libraries, archives, research institutions, technology companies, and government information agencies to explore global approaches to information access, digital preservation, privacy policies, and information equity. Through site visits and fieldwork, students analyze comparative information infrastructures, digital governance models, and cross-cultural information behaviors
ISCI 791.subject: ISCI
ISCI 791.title: Library and Information Science Study Away

ISCI 794.description: Supervised field experience in library, media center, or other information agency relevant to student’s professional goals.
ISCI 794.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in ISCI 701 and ISCI 705.
ISCI 794.subject: ISCI
ISCI 794.title: Internship in Library and Information Science

ISCI 795.description: Discussion and critical examination of selected topics of current international debate regarding information and related technologies. Topics vary by title. May be repeated a maximum of 3 times.
ISCI 795.subject: ISCI
ISCI 795.title: Special Topics in International Information Issues

ISCI 796.description: Independent study in an area of library and information science relevant to the student’s professional goals.
ISCI 796.subject: ISCI
ISCI 796.title: Independent Study in Library and Information Science

ISCI 797.description: Discussion and investigation of selected topics of current concern to the library and information profession. Specific topics to be identified by title.
ISCI 797.subject: ISCI
ISCI 797.title: Selected Topics in Librarianship and Information Services

ISCI 801.description: Seminar examining a range of issues, theories, and research questions that currently shape thinking and discourse in library and information science.
ISCI 801.subject: ISCI
ISCI 801.title: Theoretical Issues in Library and Information Science

ISCI 802.description: Seminar overviewing research methods and design, including quantitative, qualitative, and multi-method approaches.
ISCI 802.subject: ISCI
ISCI 802.title: Research Methods and Design in Information Science

ISCI 803.description: Seminar examining the historical and intellectual foundations of library and information science in relation to the nature and current roles of information organization and information transfer in societies.
ISCI 803.subject: ISCI
ISCI 803.title: Information and Society

ISCI 804.description: Seminar examining the history, trends, and current status of academic careers in library and information science, emphasizing knowledge and skills needed for successful teaching, scholarship, and service.
ISCI 804.subject: ISCI
ISCI 804.title: Preparation for Academic Careers in Library and Information Science

ISCI 805.description: Seminar in the critical and analytical study of information policy and ethical issues at the individual, institutional, and international levels. Not auditable.
ISCI 805.subject: ISCI
ISCI 805.title: Information Policy and Ethics

ISCI 806.description: Seminar examining the characteristics of communication, human information interaction, and information-seeking behavior, with emphasis on social network models, and the relationship between information-seeking behaviors and the design of communication and information systems and services. Not auditable.
ISCI 806.subject: ISCI
ISCI 806.title: Communication Processes and Information-Seeking Behavior

ISCI 809.description: Involves students in planning, managing, and evaluating colloquia, including recruiting speakers, scheduling venues, attracting audiences, conducting the sessions, and evaluating the results. May be repeated up to three times for credit.
ISCI 809.subject: ISCI
ISCI 809.title: Planning and Evaluating Colloquia In Library and Information Science

ISCI 810.description: Explores libraries and other cultural institutions as lifelong educational environments where complex human interactions take place. Over the past two years, the promising intersection of cultural organizations has been a topic of strong interest to practitioners and scholars associated with these institutions. This course introduces the interdisciplinary framework, social perspectives, and research methods required to development an understanding of this intersection, the changes that will be required as new technologies alter the way that people engage with these institutions, and the challenges that have begun to emerge as their boundaries become less defined. This type of interdisciplinary framework is needed to address these topics and address both the human information needs that impel cultural institutions and the steps and strategies by which these needs may be recognized and resolved in these information rich environments.
ISCI 810.subject: ISCI
